scoring.notes: Renewable vitals are never charged for spending. They are scored by turns under 50% (warning) and under 25% (action needed), the options lost, and whether the actor changed what it was doing at 25%.

runs.haiku-first-look-s0: Haiku 5.5 via agon play-session, scenario first-look, seed 0, fog on, 2026-11-02 (issues #670, #671, #672). Defeated tick 74.
runs.qwen-first-look-s0: qwen3.8:27b seat driver, scenario first-look, seed 0, run 20261102-173839 (issue #670). Defeated tick 159, in water.

evidence.limits: Raw run records are not in the repo (artifacts/ is ignored). Entries cite the turn logs quoted in #670-#672. Token value and the three vital-pressure numbers were not recorded by the seat driver, so they are null unless the issue text gives them.

entries.trigger: The actor stands in a field that harms it, or its health fell last turn and it did not move.
entries.action: Step to the adjacent free cell that harms least; hold only when no step is better.

evidence.note: Waited in water while health fell 20, 16, 12, 8, 4, 0.

entries.gap: reflexive already steps out of a harming field (#308), but a step needs stamina. Both losing runs reached stamina 0 first, so the reflex had nothing to spend (see keep-a-step-in-reserve).

entries.trigger: Stamina is under 25% (or cannot pay one step) and a hostile caster or a harming field is within reach.
entries.action: Stop spending stamina on anything but the step out; retreat before stamina hits 0.

evidence.note: A water push took stamina to 0 and soaked the hero; wait was the only legal action; stamina did not recover because each push soaked again.

entries.gap: The tactic has to fire above the line where retreat becomes unaffordable. Whether the rule itself (#671) should leave an always-affordable step is Darren's call and out of scope here.

entries.trigger: The same command was refused, or changed nothing, on the previous turn.
entries.action: Pick a different command from the legal list; never offer the refused one again until the position changes.

evidence.note: Diagonal moves from the legal list were refused with 'Something is in the way' several times (#672, not yet verified).

covers.operations: moveWasRefused in actor/controller.js (#457) already skips a refused move for the Actor's own proposals

entries.gap: Covers NPC moves only. A seat or ai_controlled actor gets no such memory; the legal list itself is the fix if #672 confirms a mismatch.

entries.trigger: The only unexplored way on is a corridor whose far end is unseen, and a hostile with a ranged affinity was last seen near it.
entries.action: Stop at the edge, outside the hostile's reach plus one, and look (light push/pull or inspect) before committing a step inside.

evidence.note: W1 sat in the only unexplored corridor; the hero walked into its water push at range 2 and the exit was never seen.

entries.gap: A fixed hostileWithin line is a list; choosing where to stand so a corridor is seen without entering reach is geometry over reach, line of sight and stamina, a multi-step plan. This is the case the #674 oracle should test first.

entries.trigger: The hero holds no attack and a guard covers a cell on the only known route.
entries.action: Choose the route that keeps every step outside the guard's range plus one, or turn back and look for another way.

evidence.note: The starting kit was one passive fire emit; no attack was ever offered (#670).

covers.operations: fieldUtilityRanks safety rank ranks one step at a time

entries.gap: A one-step safety rank cannot see that every route crosses the reach. This is a path-with-constraints problem; the prior probe found the policy suboptimal in 19/45 boards and 9/45 survive a rank reorder at H=6. A*/BFS is likely enough, so z3 is not assumed.

entries.trigger: An owned emit field would cover a resource the actor wants to acquire.
entries.action: Leave the emit off, or move so the field does not cover the resource, until the resource is taken.

evidence.note: The hero's own fire emit r2 burned its own resource R1 (#670).

entries.gap: Resource value is lost before it is acquired, so it lowers tokenValueAcquired directly. The take goal does not know the emit reaches it.
